claim_verdicts.evidence: "Skipping MINOR versions when upgrading is unsupported." (kubeadm-upgrade.md line 13; same on v1-34 page). The guide covers one minor step per upgrade, so two minor versions behind means two upgrades. Carried from round 1 (old claim 1).

"`kubelet` must not be newer than `kube-apiserver`." / "`kubelet` may be up to three minor versions older than `kube-apiserver` (`kubelet` < 1.25 may only be up to two minor versions older ...)" (lines 55-56). 1.34 kubelets fall under the three-version rule. Carried from round 1 (old claim 3).

"`kubectl` is supported within one minor version (older or newer) of `kube-apiserver`." (line 130). cluster-upgrade.md lines 20-22 order: "Upgrade the control plane" ... "Upgrade clients such as kubectl". Lesson now states both without the old "so" inference.

"`kubeadm upgrade apply` does the following: Checks that your cluster is in an upgradeable state: The API server is reachable; All nodes are in the `Ready` state; The control plane is healthy. Enforces the version skew policies. ... Upgrades the control plane components or rollbacks if any of them fails to come up." (lines 345-354).

Note: "`kubeadm upgrade` also automatically renews the certificates that it manages on this node. To opt-out of certificate renewal the flag `--certificate-renewal=false` can be used." (lines 179-180).

`kubeadm upgrade node` on extra control-plane nodes "Upgrades the static Pod manifests ... Upgrades the kubelet configuration"; on workers "Upgrades the kubelet configuration" (lines 358-368). The kubelet itself is a separate step: "Upgrade the kubelet and kubectl" via apt/yum, then "Restart the kubelet: sudo systemctl daemon-reload; sudo systemctl restart kubelet".

"The upgrade procedure on control plane nodes should be executed one node at a time." (line 127). Within "Upgrading control plane nodes": "Drain the node", "Upgrade kubelet and kubectl", "Uncordon the node" (lines 233-293). Skew policy: "In-place minor version `kubelet` upgrades are not supported."

upgrading-linux-nodes.md order: Upgrade kubeadm, "Call kubeadm upgrade" ("sudo kubeadm upgrade node"), "Drain the node", "Upgrade kubelet and kubectl" + "Restart the kubelet", "Uncordon the node". kubeadm-upgrade.md: "one node at a time or few nodes at a time, without compromising the minimum required capacity"; "`STATUS` column should show `Ready`".

Node conditions table: "`Ready` | `True` if the node is healthy and ready to accept pods, `False` if the node is not healthy and is not accepting pods, and `Unknown` if the node controller has not heard from the node ..." (line 47).

"`429 Too Many Requests`: the eviction is not currently allowed because of the configured PodDisruptionBudget. You may be able to attempt the eviction again later."
